name: Tearout - Sample-to-gun (Serum 2 spectral)
description: Reference checklist for turning a tonal percussion sample into a tearout gun with Serum 2's spectral oscillator, stacked overdrive, convolution, multiband compression and pitch bend. Not executable.

manual.instruction: Start with a sine sub on oscillator A. Switch oscillator B to spectral and drag in a tonal percussion sample such as a ride; pitch it down an octave.
manual.verify: The sample contributes a pitched metallic tone while the sine holds the low end.
manual.why: Oddprophet's Serum 2 sample-to-gun tutorial uses a sine sub plus a spectral oscillator loaded with a tonal percussion sample.

manual.instruction: Stack two or more overdrives for crunch. Put a splitter after the drive and route only the highs through a convolver with a medium plate impulse; adjust decay, gain and mix.
manual.verify: The top end has body and space while the sub path stays dry.
manual.why: Oddprophet stacks Serum 2 overdrives, then convolves only the split high path.

manual.instruction: Distort again after the splitter and compress with the multiband compressor. Use LFO 2 to global main tuning for short pitch bends so each hit has a downward or upward flick.
manual.verify: The gun has a controlled transient and a repeatable pitch gesture, not random drift.
manual.why: Oddprophet adds post-splitter distortion, multiband compression and an LFO pitch bend.

manual.instruction: Use the spectral scan knob to set playback speed and direction. Add a band-pass notch filter and route the spectral oscillator through it; adjust until the sample speaks.
manual.verify: Scanning changes the sample's vowel/timbre without breaking the hit.
manual.why: Oddprophet demonstrates the scan control, band-pass notch and spectral filter routing.

manual.instruction: Try different samples and warp modes. Remove or replace the sub if the sample already has weight, and tidy stereo low end after printing.
manual.verify: The recipe works beyond one sample and the low end stays mono-compatible.
manual.why: Oddprophet swaps in several samples and treats the technique as a reusable gun recipe.

manual.instruction: Resample the result and A/B it against the source. Check that the transient survives and that the sub does not fight the kick.
manual.verify: The resampled gun is punchier than the source and sits with the drums.
manual.why: The tutorial's point is a repeatable sample-to-gun transformation; resampling is the practical way to keep the result stable.

notes: Source: oddprophet, 'SERUM 2: HOW TO TURN ANY SAMPLE INTO A HEAVY DUBSTEP BASS' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRQFCUXqXr4). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because Serum 2's spectral oscillator and effects cannot be created or verified by this engine.
